import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_33_0: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_33_1: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_33_2: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN Source3_33_2 and Source3_33_0 on movie_id
df_join_1 = pd.merge(df2, df0[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# 2) JOIN the above result with Source3_33_1 on user_id
df_join_2 = pd.merge(df_join_1, df1[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Now, construct the target table with the exact schema and types:
# Target Schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Ensure correct dtypes:
df_join_2['title'] = df_join_2['title'].astype(str)
df_join_2['user_id'] = df_join_2['user_id'].astype(float)
df_join_2['movie_id'] = df_join_2['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_join_2['rating'] = df_join_2['rating'].astype(float)
df_join_2['timestamp'] = df_join_2['timestamp'].astype(float)
df_join_2['age'] = df_join_2['age'].astype(float)
df_join_2['occupation'] = df_join_2['occupation'].astype(float)

# Select columns in the order of target schema
target_df = df_join_2[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_33_2 and Source3_33_0 on movie_id
df = pd.merge(source2, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source3_33_1 on user_id
df = pd.merge(df, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that are unique identifiers:
# title (string), user_id (float but used as group key), movie_id (int)
# Aggregate other columns by mean as target shows averages
grouped = df.groupby(["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = grouped[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write output to the specified file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
